extracted.intended_audience: registrants (public companies), corporate counsel, and others preparing SEC filings subject to Regulation S-K (Items 404–407)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory disclosure requirements and the specific information that must be provided in SEC filings concerning transactions with related persons, Section 16(a) delinquencies, codes of ethics, and corporate governance (director independence, board/committee matters, and nominating committee processes). Applicable to proxy statements, registration statements, annual/quarterly reports and other Commission filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transactions with related persons — general threshold and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any transaction, since the beginning of the registrant's last fiscal year, or any currently proposed transaction, in which the registrant was or is to be a participant and the amount involved exceeds $120,000, and in which any related person had or will have a direct or indirect material interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to transactions meeting the $120,000 threshold (subject to adjustments for smaller reporting companies). See instructions for computation of amount, examples of included transactions, and exclusions. The disclosure must include specified detail items (see separate entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Related person — name and basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose the name of the related person and the basis on which the person is a related person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must clearly identify the person and why they qualify as a related person under the Item's definition (director, executive officer, nominee, immediate family member, certain security holders or their immediate family, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Related person's interest in the transaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose the related person's interest in the transaction with the registrant, including the related person's position(s) or relationship(s) with, or ownership in, a firm, corporation, or other entity that is a party to, or has an interest in, the transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe positions, relationships, and ownership that create the interest; be specific about roles and entities involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approximate dollar value of the amount involved
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose the approximate dollar value of the amount involved in the transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute the dollar value according to the Item's computation instructions (see separate computation entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approximate dollar value of related person's interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose the approximate dollar value of the amount of the related person's interest in the transaction, which shall be computed without regard to the amount of profit or loss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value the related person's interest separately from the total transaction amount and ignore profit/loss in that computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indebtedness disclosure details
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of indebtedness, disclosure of the amount involved in the transaction shall include the largest aggregate amount of principal outstanding during the period for which disclosure is provided, the amount thereof outstanding as of the latest practicable date, the amount of principal paid during the periods for which disclosure is provided, the amount of interest paid during the period for which disclosure is provided, and the rate or amount of interest payable on the indebtedness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide time-series and current amounts, payments, interest amounts and rates; follow the separate rules on exclusions and special bank-loan treatment where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other material information about transaction or related person
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide any other information regarding the transaction or the related person in the context of the transaction that is material to investors in light of the circumstances of the particular transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a catch-all requirement: include contextual facts that would be material to investors' understanding of the transaction or the related person's role/interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'related person'
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of Item 404(a), the term related person means persons in specified categories: (a) anyone who was a director or executive officer of the registrant; any nominee for director when presented in a proxy/information statement; or any immediate family member of such persons (defined by an enumerated list and household members) at any time during the period for which disclosure is required; and (b) any person who was a security holder covered by Item 403(a) or any immediate family member of such security holder when a transaction in which such person had a direct or indirect material interest occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the enumerated lists (director, executive officer, nominee, immediate family—child, parent, spouse, in-laws, siblings, household members) to determine who is a related person. See cross-references to Item 403 and §229.403(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transaction — definition (scope of what qualifies as a transaction)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of paragraph (a), a transaction includes, but is not limited to, any financial transaction, arrangement or relationship (including any indebtedness or guarantee of indebtedness) or any series of similar transactions, arrangements or relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat guarantees, loans, leases, ongoing arrangements, and series of similar transactions as transactions for disclosure purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of amount involved — leases and installments
rubrics_metrics.description: In computing the amount involved in the transaction, in the case of any lease or other transaction providing for periodic payments or installments, include the aggregate amount of all periodic payments or installments due on or after the beginning of the registrant's last fiscal year, including any required or optional payments due during or at the conclusion of the lease or other transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate future periodic payments falling within the specified period when calculating the transaction amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of amount involved — indebtedness
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of indebtedness, compute the amount by including the largest aggregate amount of all indebtedness outstanding at any time since the beginning of the registrant's last fiscal year and all amounts of interest payable on it during the last fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the peak outstanding principal during the relevant period plus interest amounts for the last fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from indebtedness calculation — ordinary course items
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain items of indebtedness may be excluded from the calculation and need not be disclosed: amounts due from the related person for purchases of goods and services subject to usual trade terms, ordinary business travel and expense payments, and other transactions in the ordinary course of business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat routine trade payables and ordinary course reimbursements as disclosable indebtedness under this Item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for certain related persons' indebtedness
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure need not be provided of any indebtedness transaction for the related persons specified in Instruction 1.b. to paragraph (a) of this Item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction 1.b. describes related persons who are security holders covered by Item 403(a) and their immediate family; indebtedness transactions involving those persons may be exempt from disclosure per this instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bank/regulation T loans — alternative limited disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If the lender is a bank, savings and loan association, or broker-dealer extending credit under Federal Reserve Regulation T and the loans are not disclosed as past due, nonaccrual or troubled debt restructurings in the consolidated financial statements, disclosure may consist of a statement that the loans to such persons: (i) were made in the ordinary course of business; (ii) were made on substantially the same terms, including interest rates and collateral, as those prevailing at the time for comparable loans with persons not related to the lender; and (iii) did not involve more than the normal risk of collectibility or present other unfavorable features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For qualifying bank-type loans, a narrative statement substituting for full detail is permitted if the loans meet the three listed conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment compensation exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of an employment relationship or transaction involving an executive officer and any related compensation solely resulting from that employment relationship need not be provided pursuant to paragraph (a) if: (i) the compensation is reported pursuant to Item 402; (ii) the executive officer is not an immediate family member and such compensation would have been reported under Item 402 as compensation earned for services to the registrant if the officer was a named executive officer and such compensation had been approved, or recommended for approval, by the compensation committee (or similar); or (iii) the transaction involves recovery of erroneously awarded compensation disclosed pursuant to Item 402(w) and applicable listing standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employment-related compensation is generally covered by Item 402; do not redundantly disclose under Item 404 if the stated conditions are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director compensation exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of compensation to a director need not be provided pursuant to paragraph (a) if the compensation is reported pursuant to Item 402(k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director compensation reported elsewhere under Item 402(k) is exempt from Item 404's separate disclosure requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a person's position or ownership does not create an indirect material interest
rubrics_metrics.description: A person shall not be deemed to have an indirect material interest where the interest arises only: (i) from such person's position as a director of another corporation or organization that is a party to the transaction; or (ii) from direct or indirect ownership by such person and other specified persons, in the aggregate, of less than a ten percent equity interest in another person (other than a partnership) which is a party; or (iii) from limited partnership interests of less than ten percent where the person is not a general partner and holds no other position in the partnership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these bright-line rules to identify when common affiliations or small ownership stakes do not create reportable indirect material interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transactions not requiring disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure need not be provided pursuant to paragraph (a) if: (a) the rates or charges involved are determined by competitive bids, or transaction involves rendering services as a common or contract carrier or public utility at rates fixed in conformity with law/governmental authority; (b) transaction involves services as a bank depositary, transfer agent, registrar, trustee under a trust indenture, or similar services; or (c) the related person's interest arises solely from ownership of a class of equity securities of the registrant and all holders of that class received the same benefit on a pro rata basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These exceptions remove from disclosure transactions that are arm's-length public-rate or purely pro rata equity benefits, and specified service-provider roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policies and procedures for review/approval/ratification of related-person transactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the registrant's policies and procedures for the review, approval, or ratification of any transaction required to be reported under paragraph (a). Examples of such features may include: the types of transactions covered; the standards to be applied; the persons or groups responsible for applying such policies/procedures; and whether such policies are in writing and, if not, how they are evidenced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient detail about governance processes, decisionmakers, and standards so investors can understand how related-person transactions are vetted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify transactions where policies were not followed
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify any transaction required to be reported under paragraph (a) since the beginning of the registrant's last fiscal year where such policies and procedures did not require review, approval or ratification or where such policies and procedures were not followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose departures from the policies/procedures described, including transactions that bypassed required review or approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal exception for prior transactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure need not be provided regarding any transaction that occurred at a time before the related person became one of the enumerated persons in Instruction 1.a.i., ii., or iii. to Item 404(a) if such transaction did not continue after the related person became one of the enumerated persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-existing transactions that ended before the person became a director/officer/nominee are exempt from disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promoter disclosure — names and consideration received
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants filing an S-1 or Form 10 that had a promoter at any time during the past five fiscal years must state the names of the promoter(s) and the nature and amount of anything of value (including money, property, contracts, options or rights of any kind) received or to be received by each promoter, directly or indirectly, from the registrant and the nature and amount of any assets, services or other consideration therefore received or to be received by the registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full disclosure about promoters' compensation and related transfers is required for registration statement filers under S-1/Form 10; include direct and indirect benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promoter-related asset acquisition disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: As to any assets acquired or to be acquired by the registrant from a promoter, state the amount at which the assets were acquired or are to be acquired and the principle followed or to be followed in determining such amount, and identify the persons making the determination and their relationship, if any, with the registrant or any promoter. If the assets were acquired by the promoter within two years prior to their transfer to the registrant, also state the cost thereof to the promoter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide pricing rationale, decisionmakers, and historical cost to the promoter where assets transferred recently prior to acquisition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure when control of shell company acquired
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the disclosure required for promoters as to any person who acquired control of a registrant that is a shell company, or any person part of a group that acquired control of a shell company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply promoter-style disclosure to persons who gain control of shell companies; see cross-reference to definitions of shell company in Rules 405/12b-2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smaller reporting companies — lower threshold and specific requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant that qualifies as a 'smaller reporting company' must provide the information required by paragraph (a) for transactions in which the amount involved exceeds the lesser of $120,000 or one percent of the average of the smaller reporting company's total assets at year end for the last two completed fiscal years; the information required by paragraph (c); and a list of all parents showing the basis of control and percentage of voting securities owned by each immediate parent, if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smaller reporting companies use a lower monetary threshold (lesser of $120k or 1% of average assets) and must also disclose parent information and promoter-related disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smaller reporting companies — underwriting and period requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Include information for any material underwriting discounts and commissions upon the sale of securities by the smaller reporting company where any of the persons specified in paragraph (a) was or is to be a principal underwriter or is a controlling person or member of a firm that was or is to be a principal underwriter. For smaller reporting companies, information shall be given for the period specified in paragraph (a) and, in addition, for the fiscal year preceding the small reporting company's last fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide extra historical period and underwriting detail for smaller reporting companies where related persons are involved in underwriting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 404 — required historical periods and foreign private issuer compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If information called for by Item 404 is presented in a registration statement, information shall be given for the periods specified in the Item and, in addition, for the two fiscal years preceding the registrant's last fiscal year, unless incorporated by reference into an S-4; a foreign private issuer will be deemed to comply if it provides the information required by Item 7.B. of Form 20-F with more detail provided if it is otherwise publicly available or required by its home jurisdiction or listing market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration statements typically require three years of disclosure (last fiscal year plus two preceding years); foreign private issuers may rely on Form 20-F content per instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delinquent Section 16(a) Reports — identification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the caption 'Delinquent Section 16(a) Reports,' identify each person who, at any time during the fiscal year, was a director, officer, beneficial owner of more than ten percent of any class of equity securities of the registrant, or any other person subject to Section 16 with respect to the registrant, that failed to file on a timely basis reports required by Section 16(a) during the most recent fiscal year or prior fiscal years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List reporting persons who had late filings; caption can be excluded if no disclosure is required (encouraged).

rubrics_metrics.name: Delinquent Section 16(a) Reports — detail on delinquencies
rubrics_metrics.description: For each such person, set forth the number of late reports, the number of transactions that were not reported on a timely basis, and any known failure to file a required form (including Form 3, Form 5, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide counts and descriptions of the nature of late filings; the registrant need only disclose a failure to file timely once (one-time disclosure rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of inquiry for Section 16(a) disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether disclosure is required, the registrant may rely only on: (1) a review of Forms 3 and 4 and amendments filed electronically with the Commission during the registrant's most recent fiscal year; (2) a review of Forms 5 and amendments filed electronically with the Commission with respect to the registrant's most recent fiscal year; and (3) any written representation from the reporting person that no Form 5 is required, which the registrant must maintain in its records for two years and make available to the Commission upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit the search to the enumerated forms/timeframes and retain any written representations for two years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of ethics — existence disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose whether the registrant has adopted a code of ethics that applies to the registrant's principal executive officer, principal financial officer, principal accounting officer or controller, or persons performing similar functions. If the registrant has not adopted such a code, explain why it has not done so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make a simple affirmative/negative disclosure and provide explanation for absence of a code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of ethics — definition and required components
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of Item 406, 'code of ethics' means written standards reasonably designed to deter wrongdoing and to promote: (1) honest and ethical conduct including handling conflicts of interest; (2) full, fair, accurate, timely, and understandable disclosure in Commission filings and public communications; (3) compliance with laws, rules and regulations; (4) the prompt internal reporting of violations to appropriate persons identified in the code; and (5) accountability for adherence to the code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the code addresses all five enumerated elements to meet the Item's definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of ethics — methods of furnishing to the Commission/public
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrant must either (1) file with the Commission a copy of its code of ethics as an exhibit to its annual report; (2) post the text of such code on its Internet website and disclose the Internet address and the fact of posting in its annual report; or (3) undertake in its annual report to provide to any person without charge, upon request, a copy of such code and explain how such request may be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of these three methods must be followed; if posting is used, disclose the URL in the annual report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of ethics — website posting of waivers/amendments option
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant intends to satisfy the disclosure requirement under Item 5.05 of Form 8-K regarding an amendment to, or a waiver from, a provision of its code of ethics by posting such information on its internet website, disclose the registrant's internet address and such intention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform investors if the registrant will use website posting to satisfy Form 8-K disclosure obligations for waivers/amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of ethics — scope and web accessibility instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant may have separate codes for different types of officers; a code of ethics may be part of a broader document; in satisfying the filing/posting/providing requirements, a registrant need only file/post/provide the portions that constitute a code of ethics as defined. If code is posted on the website, it must remain accessible on the Web site for as long as the registrant remains subject to the Item and chooses to comply by posting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the portions that meet the Item's definition need be filed/posted; ensure ongoing accessibility if posting is selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director independence identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify each director and, when disclosure is presented in a proxy/information statement relating to the election of directors, each nominee for director, that is independent under the independence standards applicable to the registrant. Also identify each director who is a member of compensation, nominating or audit committee that is not independent under such committee independence standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the registrant's applicable independence definitions and disclose identities of independent directors and any committee members who are not independent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of independence — listed and non-listed issuers
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether a director or nominee is independent, use the applicable definition of independence as follows: (i) if the registrant is a listed issuer, use the registrant's definition used for compliance with the exchange's listing standards (and committee-specific standards if applicable); (ii) if not listed, use a definition of a national securities exchange or inter-dealer quotation system which has requirements that a majority of the board be independent and state which definition is used; (iii) for registration statements applying for listing, use definitions in compliance with listing standards or the listing standards themselves if no definitions adopted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a single definition consistently for all directors and nominees and apply committee-specific standards where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrant-defined independence — disclosure of availability and appendix requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant uses its own definitions for determining independence, disclose whether these definitions are available to security holders on the registrant's Web site; if so provide the Web site address. If not, include a copy of these policies in an appendix to the registrant's proxy or information statement provided to security holders at least once every three fiscal years or if the policies have been materially amended since the beginning of the registrant's last fiscal year. If a current copy is not available, identify the most recent fiscal year in which the policies were so included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the registrant's independence definitions accessible to security holders either online or via periodic proxy/information statement appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transactions considered in determining independence — disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: For each director and nominee identified as independent, describe, by specific category or type, any transactions, relationships or arrangements not disclosed pursuant to Item 404 that were considered by the board under the applicable independence definitions in determining that the director is independent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficiently detailed descriptions of the categories/types of relationships that were evaluated in the independence determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of reliance on exchange exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant is a listed issuer that relied on exemptions to requirements that a majority of the board be independent (or if not listed but uses a market's exemptions), disclose the exemption relied upon and explain the basis for the registrant's conclusion that such exemption is applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about any reliance on exchange-provided exemptions and the rationale for such reliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of former directors
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants shall provide the disclosure required by paragraph (a) for any person who served as a director during any part of the last completed fiscal year, except no information need be given in a registration statement filed at a time when the registrant is not subject to the reporting requirements respecting any director who is no longer a director at the time of effectiveness of the registration statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include directors who served during the most recently completed fiscal year even if no longer serving, except in the registration-statement timing exception described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required detail for describing transactions/relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: The description of the specific categories or types of transactions, relationships or arrangements considered in independence determinations must be provided in such detail as is necessary to fully describe the nature of the transactions, relationships or arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Level of detail should be sufficient for investors to understand the nature and implications of the relationships considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board meetings and attendance disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: State the total number of meetings of the board of directors (including regularly scheduled and special meetings) held during the last full fiscal year and name each incumbent director who during the last full fiscal year attended fewer than 75 percent of the aggregate of (i) total board meetings (during the period they were a director) and (ii) total committee meetings on which they served (during periods served).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute attendance as an aggregate of board and committee meetings and identify directors below the 75% threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on attendance at annual meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the registrant's policy, if any, with regard to board members' attendance at annual meetings of security holders and state the number of board members who attended the prior year's annual meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the information is included on the registrant's website, the registrant may provide the website address instead of reproducing the information in the proxy statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing committees — existence, membership, meetings, and functions
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether the registrant has standing audit, nominating and compensation committees of the board of directors, or committees performing similar functions. If so, identify each committee member, state the number of committee meetings held by each such committee during the last fiscal year and describe briefly the functions performed by each such committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide committee composition, meeting frequency, and brief functional descriptions; avoid duplication of information already provided under other paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominating committee — absence disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant does not have a standing nominating committee or committee performing similar functions, state the basis for the view of the board that it is appropriate not to have such a committee and identify each director who participates in the consideration of director nominees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain governance arrangements used instead of a formal nominating committee and name participants involved in nominee consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominating committee — charter and shareholder-recommendation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether or not the nominating committee has a charter. If it has a charter, provide the disclosure required regarding the nominating committee charter. If the committee has a policy with regard to the consideration of any director candidates recommended by security holders, provide a description of the material elements of that policy, which shall include, but need not be limited to, a statement as to whether the committee will consider director candidates recommended by security holders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose charter status and any shareholder-recommendation policy elements, including whether shareholder recommendations will be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominating committee — no-policy disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If the nominating committee does not have a policy with regard to the consideration of any director candidates recommended by security holders, state that fact and state the basis for the view of the board that it is appropriate not to have such a policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the rationale for not having a shareholder-recommendation policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for security holder nominations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the nominating committee will consider candidates recommended by security holders, describe the procedures to be followed by security holders in submitting such recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide step-by-step or procedural guidance for how security holders should submit nominee recommendations (deadlines, forms, evidence required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum qualifications and desired director qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any specific minimum qualifications that the nominating committee believes must be met by a nominating-committee-recommended nominee and describe any specific qualities or skills that the nominating committee believes are necessary for one or more of the registrant's directors to possess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List substantive minimum qualifications and particular skills or attributes the committee seeks in directors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination identification and evaluation process, including diversity considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the nominating committee's process for identifying and evaluating nominees for director, including nominees recommended by security holders, and any differences in the manner in which the committee evaluates nominees based on whether recommended by a security holder, and whether, and if so how, the nominating committee (or the board) considers diversity in identifying nominees for director. If the committee (or board) has a policy regarding consideration of diversity, describe how it is implemented and how the committee (or board) assesses its effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain sourcing, evaluation criteria, any different treatment for shareholder-recommended nominees, the role of diversity policies, implementation steps, and assessment methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source identification for nominating-committee-approved nominees
rubrics_metrics.description: With regard to each nominee approved by the nominating committee for inclusion on the registrant's proxy card (other than nominees who are executive officers or directors standing for re-election), state which one or more of the following categories recommended that nominee: security holder, non-management director, chief executive officer, other executive officer, third-party search firm, or other specified source. For investment companies, additional categories apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each new/approved nominee, identify the recommending source(s) from the enumerated categories; obtain consents where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party fees related to director identification/evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant pays a fee to any third party or parties to identify or evaluate or assist in identifying or evaluating potential nominees, disclose the function performed by each such third party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify paid advisors/ search firms and describe services rendered in the nomination process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure for shareholder recommendations from >5% holders
rubrics_metrics.description: If the nominating committee received, by a date not later than the 120th calendar day before the registrant's prior year's proxy statement release date, a recommended nominee from a security holder that beneficially owned more than 5% of voting common stock for at least one year (or a group meeting the threshold), identify the candidate and the security holder/group that recommended the candidate and disclose whether the nominating committee chose to nominate the candidate, provided written consent of both the security holder/group and the candidate to be identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only disclose the identity of recommending >5% holders and nominees with written consent of both parties; follow evidence and timing rules in the Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of ownership and timing rules for >5% recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of the >5% recommendation disclosure, the percentage may be determined using the registrant's most recent reports filed with the Commission unless known to be inaccurate. If the annual meeting date has changed by more than 30 days, the obligation arises where the registrant receives the recommendation a reasonable time before printing and mailing proxy materials. If the recommending security holder is not the registered holder, they may submit (a) a written statement from the record holder verifying required ownership and holding period, or (b) copies of Schedule 13D/G or Forms 3/4/5 reflecting ownership as of or before the date of recommendation plus a written statement of continuous holding for the one-year period. The security holder/group must provide written consent of all parties to be identified at the time of recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registry may validate >5% status through public filings or broker statements; require written consents for identification; observe timing when meeting date shifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominating committee — definition/instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of paragraph (c)(2), the term 'nominating committee' refers not only to nominating committees and committees performing similar functions, but also to groups of directors fulfilling the role of a nominating committee, including the entire board of directors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the Item's requirements to any board grouping performing nominating functions, whether formally titled a committee or not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes to shareholder-nomination procedures — disclosure timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any material changes to the procedures by which security holders may recommend nominees to the registrant's board of directors, where those changes were implemented after the registrant last provided disclosure in response to the requirements. This disclosure need only be provided in a registrant's quarterly or annual reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report procedural changes to shareholder nomination processes in the next periodic report (quarterly/annual) rather than only in proxy statements.
